setup: Throwaway temp vault + empty _librarian/sessions/ + temp data/librarian.db. Drive the capture code path (the path the Stop hook would call) once with a session that produced a decision.
action: Invoke the capture code path with a single session's worth of activity, then read _librarian/sessions/<today>.md.
expected: Exactly one new summary entry for that session: a single curated/distilled line describing what the session decided or produced, NOT a dumped transcript or multi-line conversation.
pass: Deterministic gate: entry count for the session == 1. Judge rubric: the entry reads as one appraised line (not a transcript dump, not verbatim conversation). Judge <0.5 is a fail.

setup: Temp vault containing a note at Notes/foo.md with known content. Empty _librarian/sessions/.
action: Capture a session summary that names Notes/foo.md as a touched store note; read back the stored record.
expected: The reference records Notes/foo.md by versioned identity: vault-relative path PLUS a content-hash or git ref captured as-read (not path alone).
pass: Stored ref contains both the vault-relative path and a durable identity (content-hash or git ref) that reproduces from the note as-read. Path-only reference == 0.0.

setup: Temp vault + _librarian/sessions/ containing one pre-existing record file with one entry.
action: Drive the capture code path with an empty/failed hook payload (no summary content) for a new day.
expected: No entry is appended; no new empty session-record file is created for the new day; the pre-existing record and its entry are byte-unchanged.
pass: No file created at _librarian/sessions/<new-day>.md AND pre-existing record file hash unchanged. Any empty-file creation or mutation == 0.0.

setup: Temp vault + empty _librarian/sessions/. No MCP tool is invoked by the user during the session.
action: Run a session end-to-end using only the ambient capture code path; assert no user-facing tool call is required to trigger capture.
expected: Capture occurs with zero explicit in-session user action (no librarian tool call needed to record the summary).
pass: The summary entry is present after session end without any user-issued librarian tool call in the transcript. If capture requires a manual user tool invocation == 0.0.

setup: Seed three session records dated 2026-07-20, 2026-07-22, 2026-07-24, each with one entry.
action: Invoke librarian-recent with no window.
expected: Entries returned most-recent-first by session date: 2026-07-24, 2026-07-22, 2026-07-20.
pass: Returned order equals reverse-chronological by session date. Ordering scored as fraction of correctly ordered adjacent pairs.

setup: Seed one session record dated 2026-07-24 whose entry references Notes/foo.md by path+hash.
action: Invoke librarian-recent; inspect each returned entry.
expected: Each returned entry shows its session date AND the versioned provenance (path + content-hash/git ref) of referenced notes.
pass: Every returned entry carries its date and, where it references a note, the versioned identity. Missing date or bare-path provenance == 0.0.

setup: Seed 10 session records spanning 2026-07-10 through 2026-07-24.
action: Invoke librarian-recent with a 7-day window (and separately with count=3).
expected: Window restricts results to records within the last 7 days; count=3 returns exactly the 3 most recent.
pass: Windowed result set == records within window; count-limited result == exactly N most-recent. Either limit ignored == 0.0.

setup: Empty _librarian/sessions/ (no records at all).
action: Invoke librarian-recent.
expected: An explicit empty-state message is returned (e.g. no recent sessions recorded yet), not an error and not an empty/ambiguous response.
pass: Response is a non-error, human-legible empty-state message. Thrown error or empty/blank payload == 0.0.

setup: Temp vault with Notes/foo.md indexed for S1 FTS. Seed a session record referencing Notes/foo.md with a conclusion dated 2026-07-22.
action: Run librarian-search for a query that returns Notes/foo.md; inspect that result.
expected: The result for Notes/foo.md carries a prior-engagement annotation naming what Robin concluded/touched and when, reading as an additive signal (not a re-rank, not a nag).
pass: Deterministic gate: the referenced result has an annotation containing the prior engagement + its date. Judge rubric: annotation reads as additive prior-engagement metadata, not a directive/nag. Judge <0.5 is a fail.

setup: Temp vault with Notes/foo.md and Notes/bar.md indexed; a session record references ONLY Notes/foo.md.
action: Run a search returning both notes; inspect the Notes/bar.md result.
expected: Notes/bar.md (no referencing session record) carries NO annotation - quiet when unprompted, no not-seen-before noise.
pass: Unreferenced result has zero prior-engagement annotation. Any annotation on the unreferenced result == 0.0.

setup: Same temp vault/index used for an S1 baseline search snapshot of a fixed query. Then seed a session record referencing one of the results.
action: Run the identical query with enrichment enabled; capture result membership and ranking order; diff against the S1 baseline snapshot.
expected: Result-set membership and ranking order are identical to the un-enriched S1 search; only additive annotation metadata differs.
pass: Membership set equal AND ranking order equal to S1 baseline for the same query. Any add/drop/reorder == 0.0.

setup: Temp _librarian/ with an empty stateful-use log.
action: Invoke librarian-recent once; read the stateful-use log.
expected: Exactly one timestamped stateful-use event is appended.
pass: Log gains exactly one event with a parseable timestamp. Zero or >1 events == 0.0.

setup: Temp vault/index + a session record referencing a note that a query will surface. Empty stateful-use log.
action: Run a librarian-search that surfaces at least one prior-engagement signal; then run a search that surfaces none; read the log.
expected: The signal-bearing search appends exactly one timestamped event; the no-signal search appends none.
pass: Exactly one event from the signal-bearing search AND zero from the no-signal search. Otherwise == 0.0.

setup: Seed a stateful-use log with events across three ISO weeks (2 in W29, 4 in W30, 1 in W31), each timestamped.
action: Query the per-ISO-week count over the date range covering all three weeks.
expected: Per-ISO-week counts derive correctly (W29=2, W30=4, W31=1); every invocation is timestamped so manual wish-log review of unprompted use is supportable.
pass: Returned weekly buckets equal the seeded counts AND every logged event carries a timestamp. Any miscount or untimestamped event == 0.0.

setup: A freshly captured session record at _librarian/sessions/2026-07-24.md.
action: Parse the record frontmatter and validate it against a typed schema (required keys and value types).
expected: Frontmatter parses cleanly and contains the typed fields a mdbase collection would require (a date/day, session/entry identity, and a typed refs list), with correct scalar/list types.
pass: Frontmatter parses as YAML into a typed object with required keys present and correctly typed. Missing/mistyped required field == 0.0.

setup: A record whose frontmatter includes a refs list with versioned identities.
action: Validate the refs field shape against the mdbase-compatible collection schema (list of typed ref objects, no untyped coercion, no unknown-shape acceptance).
expected: refs is a list of typed reference entries (path + hash/git-ref); the schema rejects a scalar-where-list or list-where-scalar mismatch.
pass: refs validates as a typed list AND a deliberately malformed refs shape is rejected by the schema. Otherwise == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault. Drive the capture code path once for session S with directive D (summary+refs); record the resulting day file bytes.
action: Invoke the capture code path 4 more times for the same session S with the identical directive D (simulating Stop firing at the end of each subsequent assistant turn), then re-read the day file.
expected: The day record is byte-identical to its state after the first capture: exactly one entry for session S, no duplicates, no rewritten timestamps.
pass: byte-compare(after_first, after_fifth) == identical AND entry count for session S == 1. Any appended duplicate == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault. Capture session S with directive D1, then capture session S again with a changed directive D2 (different summary).
action: Read the day record and enumerate entries for session S.
expected: Two entries for session S — D1's entry preserved unmodified, D2's entry appended after it (last-directive-wins as revision, never overwrite/delete per INV-3).
pass: entries(S) == [D1, D2] in order AND D1's bytes unmodified. In-place mutation or deletion of D1 == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault. A Stop-shaped capture payload carrying a cwd that lies inside a git working tree whose .git/config declares a remote origin URL.
action: Drive the capture entry point with the payload; read back the appended entry's frontmatter.
expected: The entry carries workspace provenance derived with zero user action: the cwd verbatim (inert), a project name automatically extracted from the cwd, and the repository remote identity read from .git/config.
pass: workspace.cwd, workspace.project (auto-derived, non-empty), and workspace.repo (matching the config remote) all present and typed. Any user-supplied naming requirement or missing field == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault. Two capture payloads: (a) one with NO cwd at all; (b) one whose cwd is a real directory with no enclosing .git anywhere up the tree.
action: Drive capture with both payloads; read back both entries.
expected: (a) captures normally with the workspace field wholly absent; (b) captures normally with cwd+project present and repo omitted. Neither capture fails, blocks, or writes a partial/placeholder provenance shape.
pass: Both entries append successfully; (a) has no workspace key, (b) has workspace without repo. Any capture failure or placeholder value == 0.0.

setup: A day record written by the pre-v3.1.0 code (entries with no workspace field, schema session-record@1), then a new v3.1.0 capture appended into the SAME day file.
action: Parse and schema-validate the resulting mixed record; enumerate entries.
expected: The mixed record validates against session-record@1 (no schema-id bump, no migration): the old entry remains byte-preserved without workspace, the new entry carries it. readAllRecords/librarian-recent consume both.
pass: Mixed record validates; old entry unmodified; both entries readable. Schema-id bump, migration requirement, or old-record rejection == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault. Capture session S with directive D and cwd W1; record the day-file bytes.
action: Re-drive capture 3 more times for session S with identical directive D but cwd varied (W1, a renamed W2, and absent), then re-read the file.
expected: All re-fires are idempotent no-ops: the record stays byte-identical to the first capture. Provenance differences alone never create a new entry (idempotence keys on directive content, not workspace).
pass: byte-compare(after_first, after_fourth) == identical AND entries(S) == 1. Any provenance-triggered append == 0.0.

setup: Seed session records spanning three projects ('my-librarian', 'novel', 'ks-research') plus one pre-v3.1.0 entry with no workspace.
action: Invoke librarian-recent unfiltered, then with project filter 'Novel' (case differs).
expected: Unfiltered: every provenance-carrying entry displays its project name; the provenance-less entry displays quietly with no placeholder. Filtered: exactly the 'novel' entries return (case-insensitive match); the provenance-less entry is excluded, not fabricated into a match; ordering rule unchanged.
pass: Display and filter behavior exactly as expected including case-insensitivity and quiet legacy entry. Placeholder noise, wrong membership, or re-ordering == 0.0.

setup: The built server as constructed for stdio serving (no client-side configuration anywhere).
action: Inspect the MCP initialize result / server construction for declared server-level instructions.
expected: The server declares non-empty MCP instructions that (a) name librarian-recent for recency questions, (b) name librarian-search for prior-engagement/content questions, and (c) direct clients to consult them before reading files directly.
pass: Instructions present at the MCP server level and contain all three elements. Absent instructions, or guidance living only in client config/docs == 0.0.

setup: The built server as constructed for stdio serving (no client-side configuration anywhere).
action: Inspect the MCP initialize result / server construction for the declared server-level instructions.
expected: The instructions include a plain-language authoring style contract for librarian-session summary directives carrying all four normative elements: (a) write for a later reader without this session's context, (b) lead with what was decided or produced, (c) prefer common words over session shorthand, (d) expand or avoid session-local codenames/version tags/abbreviations. Wording may vary; all four elements must be present and tied to authoring the directive summary.
pass: All four elements present in the server-level instructions. Any element missing, or the contract living only in docs/client config == 0.0.

setup: The built server as constructed for stdio serving.
action: Inspect the declared server-level instructions for read-time guidance.
expected: The instructions direct clients to report recalled session summaries (librarian-recent output, prior-engagement annotations) in plain language for the asking reader, and this guidance applies to records authored before the contract existed (read-time is the only layer that reaches pre-contract records).
pass: Render-in-plain-language guidance present and not scoped to only new records. Absent, or scoped so legacy records are excluded == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault. A directive whose summary flagrantly violates the style contract: 300+ words of dense build-log jargon, invented codenames, version tags, control-adjacent punctuation-heavy shorthand.
action: Drive capture with the violating directive, then read the day-file and invoke librarian-recent.
expected: Capture succeeds normally. The stored summary is byte-identical to the submitted summary (no rewrite, no truncation, no rejection, no style warning injected into the record). librarian-recent returns the stored text unmodified.
pass: byte-compare(submitted_summary, stored_summary) == identical AND capture exit success AND recent output contains the stored text verbatim. Any server-side rewrite/truncation/rejection == 0.0.

setup: Throwaway temp vault + _librarian/ + temp data/librarian.db, no pre-existing _librarian/note-identity.md. A session entry references note A by vault-relative path notes/a.md plus content hash H. Note A has since been renamed to notes/archive/a.md with its content byte-unchanged (still hashes to H); no other current vault note hashes to H.
action: Run a reindex, then read _librarian/note-identity.md.
expected: The ledger exists at _librarian/note-identity.md with mdbase-compatible frontmatter under schema note-identity@1 and carries exactly one appended binding for the dead ref, bearing all six fields: an identity id, from-path notes/a.md, to-path notes/archive/a.md, content hash H, a timestamp, and detected: exact-hash.
pass: Ledger parses AND exactly one binding is present AND all six fields are present and correctly valued (from/to/hash match the fixture, detected == exact-hash). Any missing field, wrong provenance value, or no binding at all == 0.0.

setup: Two independent throwaway trees seeded byte-identically from the same fixture (one dead ref, exactly one exact-hash candidate), each rooted at a different directory path with its own empty temp data/librarian.db.
action: Reindex each tree in a fresh process at a different wall-clock time, then compare the resulting bindings field-by-field, ignoring only the timestamp field. Inspect the identity code path for similarity scoring, ranked candidate selection, or model invocation.
expected: Both runs produce the same binding for the same input state (same from-path, to-path, hash, detected: exact-hash). The decision depends on exact hash equality alone — no similarity score, no ranked guess, no clock- or filesystem-ordering dependence, and no inference (INV-6).
pass: Bindings identical across runs on every field except timestamp AND no similarity/heuristic score and no model call on the identity path. Any divergence between runs, or any non-hash signal influencing the binding == 0.0.

setup: A day-file session entry referencing notes/a.md@H, byte-snapshotted before the run. Note A has been renamed to notes/archive/a.md content-unchanged and a reindex has appended the exact-hash binding.
action: Invoke librarian-recent over the window and run a librarian-search whose result set includes notes/archive/a.md; then byte-compare the day-file against its snapshot.
expected: Both read surfaces resolve the recorded ref through the ledger binding and surface the prior engagement against the note's current path notes/archive/a.md, while the stored session entry's bytes are unchanged — resolution is read-time and ledger-mediated, with no retrofit of the stored ref (INV-3).
pass: librarian-recent output AND the search prior-engagement annotation both reference the current path AND byte-compare(before, after) == identical. Surfacing only the dead path, failing to annotate the renamed note, or any mutation of the stored entry == 0.0.

setup: A vault + _librarian/ tree whose ledger holds one exact-hash binding, plus one unresolved multi-candidate ref, and a fully built data/librarian.db. Dump the identity projection tables first as the reference.
action: Delete data/librarian.db entirely, reindex from vault + _librarian/ alone, and dump the identity projection tables again.
expected: The identity projection tables are rebuilt in full from vault + _librarian/ sidecar alone and match the reference dump (same bindings, same unresolved refs with the same candidate sets). No load-bearing identity state lived only in the database (INV-4).
pass: Post-rebuild identity projection == reference projection AND reindex completes with no missing-state error. Any binding, candidate set, or unresolved record that cannot be reconstructed from vault + sidecar == 0.0.

setup: A vault + _librarian/ tree containing one resolvable dead ref, one zero-candidate ref, and one multi-candidate ref; ledger byte-snapshotted.
action: Reindex, then dump and hash the identity projection tables using a canonically ordered dump; reindex a second time with no vault or sidecar change; dump and hash again. Byte-compare _librarian/note-identity.md across both runs.
expected: The two identity projections are byte-identical, and the second reindex leaves the ledger byte-unchanged — an already-recorded binding is not re-appended, and nothing is reordered.
pass: hash(dump_1) == hash(dump_2) AND ledger byte-identical after the second reindex. Any projection drift, duplicate re-append, or reordering == 0.0.

setup: A session entry references notes/b.md@H2. Note B has been renamed AND edited, so no current vault note hashes to H2. Ledger byte-snapshotted (or absent).
action: Reindex, then read _librarian/note-identity.md and the identity projection's unresolved-ref records.
expected: The ref is recorded as unresolved with an empty candidate set and no binding is appended (constitution prohibition 8: never auto-bind an ambiguous match). The ledger gains no entry for this ref.
pass: An unresolved record exists for notes/b.md with an empty candidate set AND zero bindings were appended for it. Any binding — to the renamed-and-edited note or anything else == 0.0.

setup: A session entry references notes/c.md@H3. notes/c.md no longer resolves, and three current vault notes (notes/x.md, notes/dup/x.md, archive/x-copy.md) all carry content hashing to H3.
action: Reindex, then read the ledger and the unresolved-ref record with its candidate set.
expected: The ref is recorded as unresolved listing every candidate (all three), and no binding is appended — duplicate content is ambiguity, not a tie to break.
pass: The unresolved record lists exactly the three candidate paths, complete and unelided, AND zero bindings were appended. Any binding, or a truncated/first-only/partial candidate set == 0.0.

setup: Seeded state across two day-files: one ref resolved through a binding, one unresolved zero-candidate ref, and one unresolved multi-candidate ref with three candidates.
action: Invoke librarian-recent over the window covering both day-files, and run search enrichment against a query whose results include the three candidate notes.
expected: Both read surfaces render each unresolved ref explicitly as unresolved together with its candidate set (an empty candidate set stated as such) — never omitted from output and never silently bound to a candidate. A candidate is not annotated as prior engagement.
pass: Every unresolved ref appears in librarian-recent output labeled unresolved with its candidates AND enrichment annotates no candidate-only note as prior engagement. A silently dropped unresolved ref, or a silent binding at render time == 0.0.

setup: A ledger already holding two detected: exact-hash bindings, byte-snapshotted, plus one unresolved multi-candidate ref awaiting human confirmation.
action: Supply a human confirmation selecting one candidate for the unresolved ref, then re-read the ledger.
expected: A third entry is appended attributed detected: confirmed and carrying all six fields (identity id, from-path, to-path, content hash, timestamp, provenance). The two earlier entries are byte-preserved in their original order; nothing is rewritten, reordered, or compacted.
pass: The new entry is present with detected == confirmed and all six fields AND the pre-confirmation ledger bytes are an unchanged prefix of the new file. Any edit, reorder, or compaction of earlier entries, or a confirmed binding attributed exact-hash == 0.0.

setup: A _librarian/note-identity.md containing at least one detected: exact-hash binding and one detected: confirmed binding.
action: Parse the ledger frontmatter and validate it against a typed schema for the note-identity@1 collection (required keys and value types); then validate two deliberately malformed variants — a scalar where the bindings list is required, and an entry whose detected value is a third kind (e.g. 'heuristic').
expected: The frontmatter parses cleanly as YAML into a typed object declaring schema note-identity@1, with bindings as a list of typed entries (identity id, from-path, to-path, content hash, timestamp scalar, detected constrained to exactly exact-hash | confirmed). Both malformed variants are rejected.
pass: The valid ledger validates AND both the scalar-where-list mismatch and the out-of-enum detected value are rejected. Any missing/mistyped required field, untyped coercion, or acceptance of a third provenance kind == 0.0.
